source.title: Escaping Parameter Space: Tight Generalization Bounds via Representation Quality
source.authors: N. Göring; Shuo Zhang; B. DeMoss; Ard A. Louis

record.tranche_reason: The study varies label-corruption levels and measures test error in a width sweep, a different experimental setup from the original random-label fitting intervention.
record.gate_note: The width-sweep experiment uses 0%, 10%, and 20% label noise; the text describes noise shifting Q1 upward but supplies no exact test-error values for those conditions. Other random-label findings are cited prior work, not this study's results. The SVHN representation-repulsion experiment deliberately induces memorization and is recorded as a finding about the claim's subject, not as evidence that networks naturally fit random labels.
record.test_reason: Figure 2 measures network test error across 0%, 10%, and 20% random-label replacement in a CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 width sweep, bearing on V4's test-error component. The supplied text does not establish the ordering of test error across corruption levels or perfect training fit. The SVHN intervention does not test random-label fitting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the SVHN intervention: the authors interpret preserved training accuracy alongside degraded class geometry and test accuracy as evidence that local class geometry contributes causally to generalization. This is not evidence of fitting random labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates representation certificates and a representation-repulsion intervention, not the original random-label fitting protocol. The width sweep uses 0%, 10%, and 20% label noise.
record.method_sensitivity: The SVHN intervention's trajectories differ quantitatively across ReLU, SiLU, GELU, and tanh, though the authors describe the qualitative pattern as invariant.

fits_no_version.finding: Across four activations, representation repulsion on true-label SVHN preserves near-100% training accuracy while test accuracy degrades toward chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deliberately damaging within-class representation geometry can impair generalization while preserving training-set memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: The width sweep reports label noise shifting the representation-quality term upward; the weight-noise diagnostic reports greater robustness of representation decoding than of network predictions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation quality and readout robustness vary with label corruption and parameter perturbations.

record.problems: The label-noise width-sweep outcomes are presented in Figure 2 without exact text values; the cited randomized-label fitting results are prior work. The SVHN memorization behavior is induced by a regularizer and does not establish spontaneous fitting of random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows extracted for Figure 2: the text describes Q1 shifts and the double-descent pattern but gives no exact test-error outcomes by label-noise condition; figure-only values cannot be reconstructed from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error on those labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative fitting time and convergence speed across label-corruption levels.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit at each corruption level, corruption beyond 20% through complete randomization, and approach to chance. Test-error ordering across the tested noise levels cannot be determined from the supplied figure text.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevents random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 2 is already declared in rows_left_out, so it is not added to missing. Its test-error values and ordering across noise levels are unreadable in the supplied text; no V4 verdict is justified. The reported Q1 shift cannot substitute for network test error. References to random-label fitting in Appendix B describe prior work.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random labeling experiment or training-error result.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed across corruption levels.
No shuffled-pixel or Gaussian-noise input experiment.

The width sweep measures test error at 0%, 10%, and 20% label noise, but exact figure values are unavailable in the text. It does not test corruption through 100% or report perfect training accuracy at each noise level.
No test of whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevents fitting random labels or affects true-label generalization in that setting.
No comparison of the learning order or dynamics for real versus random labels.

rows.subject: six-layer FFNN (width=1024), ReLU
rows.operation_detail: Trained with cross-entropy plus representation-repulsion regularizer Lrep, λ=2500.
rows.value: figure only; text says it saturates near 100%
rows.note: The regularizer deliberately damages local class geometry; this is not random-label fitting.
rows.check: Near-100% training accuracy is correctly reported, but uses true SVHN labels with deliberately induced representation repulsion; it cannot establish any claim version. The regularizer ramps from zero after epoch 5 to λ=2500 after epoch 505.
